steps.what: Diagnose and treat hospital inpatients at the bedside
Provide continuous care to hospital inpatients through the stay

tasks.design: She diagnoses, treats and provides continuous care to hospital inpatients at the bedside. The examination and the speech are live and no version is filed. Nothing lists the ward, drafts the clinical note, or sends an alert.
tasks.previous_blocker: The diagnosis and the treatment have to fit this inpatient in the room.
tasks.enabler_now: No tool is added, because the bedside care still needs her.
tasks.still_hard: A wrong diagnosis or treatment can harm the inpatient.
tasks.human_edge: She examines this inpatient and decides the treatment in the room.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. She still diagnoses, treats and provides continuous care herself.

reach.task: Continue the inpatient care the hospitalist set
reach.learn: Which treatment she started and what to watch on the ward

evidence.claim: Diagnosis and treatment of a hospital inpatient stay with the hospitalist. This is model knowledge.

assumptions: The upkeep allowance is zero because no tool is added.
The patient is outside the organisation. Examination, treatment and continuous care are done at the bedside and no version is filed, so both steps stay act_external and ungated.
Nothing lists the ward, drafts the clinical note, or sends an alert.
unknowns: Whether a later note is written by someone else is unknown, and this task does not file one.
research_questions: On a ward day, how much of this task is bedside examination and how much is later conversation with the same inpatient?

incremental.description: No upkeep, because no tool is added to this task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Both ends are zero. She still diagnoses, treats and provides continuous care, and no tool is added.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Prescribe medications and treatment regimens in the patient record
Compare the named inpatient regimen on the medication database
Judge that comparison before prescribing for hospital inpatients
File prescription v1 for the hospital inpatients

tasks.design: She writes the drug name, dose and route in the patient record {OTHER}. A deterministic comparison on the medication database {OTHER} then checks interactions, contraindications, doses and duplicates. She reads that comparison and still decides, then files prescription v1 herself in the patient record. Nothing lists drugs, raises an alert, or sends the order.
tasks.previous_blocker: The regimen has to be chosen for this inpatient, and a comparison cannot issue the prescription.
tasks.enabler_now: When the drug name, dose and route are already written, the interaction, contraindication, dose and duplicate comparison is a rule check.
tasks.still_hard: A wrong regimen can harm the inpatient, and the comparison does not choose the drug.
tasks.human_edge: She decides whether this inpatient should receive the regimen she named.
tasks.altitude: She no longer does that comparison by hand when the three fields are present. She still chooses the regimen, still reads the comparison, and still files prescription v1.

reach.task: Dispense from the prescription she signed
reach.learn: The drug, dose and route on prescription v1

evidence.claim: The G-Standaard checks interactions, contraindications, doses and duplicates.
Under the cited definition of a recept, a prescription is an order from a practitioner.
The hospitalist still chooses the regimen and still signs. The comparison does not prescribe. This is model knowledge.

assumptions: Reading the comparison is already her full time in s3, so the upkeep allowance on top of that is zero.
Today she compares interactions, contraindications, doses and duplicates herself, so the baseline actor on that step stays the hospitalist. The machine is only the future of that comparison.

She writes three fields in s1: drug name, dose and route. Those are the only inputs to the comparison. If any field is missing, the comparison does not run and she compares by hand. Capture of the three fields is her time in s1.
The medication database is a reference set maintained outside this task. That upkeep is not counted as time saved here.

s1 is the working regimen, not the standing prescription. Prescription v1 is filed in s4 by the hospitalist, inside the ward patient record, and it is not sent onward. Ward pharmacists are inside the organisation, so the file stays write_internal.
Nothing lists drugs, raises an alert, or sends the order.
unknowns: How often the drug name, dose or route is missing when she reaches the comparison is unknown.
research_questions: On a week of inpatient prescriptions, how often are drug name, dose and route already written before she compares interactions?

incremental.description: No separate upkeep, because reading the comparison sits entirely in the review she already does.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The task gives no minute split. Low is a prescription where the drug name, dose or route is missing, so she compares by hand and the check does not run. High is a prescription where those three fields are present and only that comparison drops. She still chooses, still reads the comparison, and still files prescription v1.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Order laboratory tests and radiographs in the patient record
Interpret the results of laboratory tests and radiographs for hospital inpatients

tasks.design: She orders the laboratory tests and radiographs herself in the patient record {OTHER}, and she interprets every result herself. Nothing drafts the interpretation, lists the results, or sends a report.
tasks.previous_blocker: The test and the reading have to fit this inpatient.
tasks.enabler_now: No tool is added, because she still chooses the test and still reads every result.
tasks.still_hard: A missed reading of a laboratory result or a radiograph can harm the inpatient.
tasks.human_edge: She decides what the result means for this inpatient.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. She still orders the tests and still interprets every result.

reach.task: Carry out the radiograph she ordered
reach.learn: Which radiograph order v1 asks for, not her interpretation

evidence.claim: Ordering a test and interpreting the result stay with the hospitalist. This is model knowledge.

assumptions: The upkeep allowance is zero because no tool is added.
The in-hospital laboratory and the radiographers are inside the organisation. Order v1 stays in the patient record, so the order is write_internal. She files it herself.
She still opens and reads every result. That reading is not shortened. Nothing drafts the interpretation, lists the results, or sends a report.
No separate interpretation document is filed in this task.
unknowns: Whether some radiographs are read first by a radiologist is unknown, and this task still keeps her own reading.
research_questions: Which of these orders in a week are laboratory tests, and which are radiographs she also reads herself?

incremental.description: No upkeep, because no tool is added to this task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Both ends are zero. She still places order v1 and still interprets every laboratory result and radiograph, and no tool is added.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Decide to admit patients for these hospital stays
Tell the patients they are admitted for the hospital stay

tasks.design: She decides whether to admit the patient and tells the patient. The decision is spoken and no version is filed. Nothing lists beds, drafts the admission note, or sends an acceptance.
tasks.previous_blocker: The admission has to fit this patient now.
tasks.enabler_now: No tool is added, because the decision and the conversation still need her.
tasks.still_hard: A wrong admission decision can harm the patient or delay care.
tasks.human_edge: She judges whether this patient needs a hospital stay.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. She still decides the admission and still tells the patient.

reach.task: Take the admitted patient onto the ward
reach.learn: That she admitted this patient for a hospital stay

evidence.claim: The admission decision and telling the patient stay with the hospitalist. This is model knowledge.

assumptions: The upkeep allowance is zero because no tool is added.
The patient is outside the organisation. Telling the patient is live speech and no version is filed, so that step stays act_external and ungated. The decision itself does not write, so it stays read.
Nothing lists beds, drafts the admission note, or sends an acceptance.
unknowns: Whether an admission record is later filed by someone else is unknown, and this task does not file one.
research_questions: How often is the admission decision spoken only to the patient, and how often does someone else later write it down?

incremental.description: No upkeep, because no tool is added to this task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Both ends are zero. She still decides the admission and still tells the patient, and no tool is added.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week is unchanged except she no longer compares interactions, contraindications, doses and duplicates by hand when the drug name, dose and route are already written. She still diagnoses, treats, provides continuous care, interprets every result, admits every patient, and signs every prescription.
reach: An acute care nurse continues the inpatient care she set.
A pharmacist dispenses from the prescription she signed.
A radiologic technologist carries out the radiograph she ordered.
A registered nurse takes the admitted patient onto the ward.
skills_to_grow: State the diagnosis in the room with the patient.
Sign only the regimen she still chooses after reading the comparison.
Read a radiograph herself before she treats from it.
role.ambitious_version: She still diagnoses, treats, interprets every result and admits every patient herself, and she signs only a regimen she chose.
